rationale:
Applies card c31 (SOAP) to p33. Only build_optimizer changes; architecture, hparams, cosine schedule and 1.0 clipping stay the same.

SOAP params: every 2-D matrix inside `blocks.*` (per-head q/k/v, attention proj, MLP up/down). Betas (0.95, 0.95), shampoo_beta = beta2, preconditioner refreshed every 10 steps with full two-sided rotation, weight decay 0.1 applied decoupled after the update, as in the official code.

Adam params: everything else (tied embedding/head, position table, 3-D Canon convs, LayerNorms, biases) keeps the same Adam rule, hand-written in the same class: betas (0.9, 0.999), eps 1e-8, same decay/no-decay split.

Build: one `torch.optim.Optimizer` subclass with a per-group `soap` flag, so `param_groups`, `zero_grad` and `state_dict` work normally and the loop's LR writes reach every group. SOAP follows nikhilvyas/SOAP:
- Step 1 only accumulates GGᵀ and GᵀG, then uses `eigh` to get bases Q sorted by descending eigenvalue.
- Later steps project the gradient (QLᵀ G QR) and keep Adam's second moment in that basis. The first moment stays in the original space and is projected. The ratio is projected back; step size is lr·√(1−β2ᵗ)/(1−β1ᵗ).
- Every 10 steps Q is refreshed by one power-iteration step plus QR, after re-sorting by estimated eigenvalues and permuting exp_avg_sq to match.

Why: Adam is diagonal, so it ignores row/column correlations in weight matrices. Shampoo's Kronecker-factored preconditioner captures them, and running Adam in its eigenbasis gives a better-conditioned update while keeping per-coordinate adaptivity, so the 3e-3 LR should roughly carry over.

Cost: matrices are at most 1024 per side, so the largest job is a 1024² eigendecomposition or QR every 10 steps plus small matmuls. Added time is moderate against a large wall-clock margin.
